steps.what: Establish actual electromechanical or pneumatic device behaviour, sensor and actuator interfaces, timing, fault states and control requirements
Design and develop control circuits or algorithms in the control-engineering category of {OTHER}, selecting logic and reusing native circuit or function blocks where applicable
Verify circuit behaviour and algorithm response on a safely isolated bench, including sensor faults, actuator limits and pneumatic delays; capture actual results
Assess test results, revise and retest as necessary, then check the final control design and its test record and limitations in the control-engineering category of {OTHER}
Commit the exact checked control design and test snapshot in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native circuit and function-block reuse in the control-engineering category of {OTHER}. The engineer still chooses logic, verifies actual device response, tests on an isolated bench and checks the final design before its versioned commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated circuit and control-block setup can require manual recreation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reusable blocks can reduce structure entry without deciding fault behaviour.
tasks.still_hard: Timing, instability, physical tolerances and failure behaviour need engineering verification.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises when a logically correct controller behaves badly on the actual device.

ambition.what: No autonomous live installation or safety-function approval.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated control setup, unchanged design authority.

reach.task: Verify actual sensor and actuator wiring
reach.learn: Trace a control assumption to the physical interface.

evidence.claim: Native control blocks can reuse circuit or algorithm structure while device behaviour still requires testing.

assumptions: Boundary is a design-and-development instance of this disjunctive task, through a checked design version and isolated bench verification. Live implementation is a separate authorised change and earns no saving here; software never commands production equipment in this proposal.

The engineer verifies device ID, input/output type, units, ranges, response time, safe state and fault cases in s1 and captures actual design values in s2. Existing design owners supply validated block definitions. Missing interface data require manual measurement or clarification, counted in s1-s3.

Native reuse first; illustrative shares are not measured baselines. Test runtime earns no labour saving. Actual test capture and final design review remain counted. The final snapshot exists before s4 concludes; edits require retesting before s5.
unknowns: Which native blocks already cover repeated structures
research_questions: How much authoring is genuinely repeated rather than new control logic?

already_counted.description: Control authoring review and final design and test assessment remain in s2 and s4.

incremental.description: Revalidate reused blocks after interface or engineering-platform changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final control design and corresponding test record checked in s4; any edit voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated block setup saves 6 gross hours less 1.5 upkeep for 4.5 net. Existing reuse or novel control logic gives zero gain. Physical work, tests, review and commit retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define mechatronics component requirements for the computer-controlled product, including mechanical envelope, sensors, electrical interfaces and intended operating conditions
Design mechatronics component geometry and mechanical interfaces in the computer-aided design category of {OTHER}, reusing native features and standard interface dimensions
Develop sensor, actuator and electronic interface layout in the electronic-design category of {OTHER}, using native pin and connector libraries while checking actual compatibility
Test integrated fit, loads, signal behaviour and tolerances using actual prototype evidence where required; write and check the final component design, test evidence and limitations
Commit the exact checked component design snapshot in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native geometry features and electronic pin and connector libraries in the relevant design categories of {OTHER}. Reuse structure while the engineer selects and validates the actual mechanical, sensing and electrical interfaces, then commits the exact checked component design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated features and interface layouts can be redrawn manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native parametrised features and component libraries can reuse known structure.
tasks.still_hard: Fit, tolerances, signal integrity and cross-domain interactions remain product-specific.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer understands how mechanical and electrical changes affect the computer-controlled product together.

ambition.what: No production release or regulated-product approval is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated drawing, unchanged component design responsibility.

reach.learn: Relate a component interface to actual manufacturing capability.

evidence.claim: Native geometry and connector libraries can reduce repeated design entry without proving integrated product suitability.

assumptions: Boundary is a component-design assignment through a checked internal version, not a manufacturing release, safety certification or installation. Prototype manufacture by other roles is an input and earns no saving here; the engineer's physical tests and capture remain counted.

Product owners supply operating envelope and interface requirements. The engineer verifies and enters dimensions, tolerances, loads, power, signal levels, pin mapping and source data-sheet versions in s1-s3. Missing values require manual investigation and are not populated from an unrelated product variant.

Native features first. Shares are an illustrative repeated-interface scenario, not measured baseline. Final s4 checking follows completed design and actual test evidence; changes void the version-bound commit approval.
unknowns: How much component structure already uses native libraries
research_questions: Which repeated features can be reused while exposing changed product assumptions?

already_counted.description: Geometry, electrical interface and final integration review remain in s2-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain and revalidate shared feature and connector definitions.

approvals.approved_version: Final integrated component design and corresponding test evidence checked in s4; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Geometry and interface reuse saves 10.5 gross hours less 2 upkeep for 8.5 net. Existing native libraries or novel designs give zero gain. Requirements, tests, engineering judgement and commit keep their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated geometry and control structures can shrink while integrated physical judgement remains central.
reach: Work with electromechanical technicians and mechanical designers on actual interfaces.
role.ambitious_version: A mechatronics engineer who reuses proven structures while testing every changed device assumption.
